# Multiple Attempts for Ungraded Text Entry Questions (Survey)

Hello,

I have a lesson designed with ungraded text entry questions. They serve as more of a guided exercise, rather than an assignment--there are "right" answers, but we aren't trying to assess whether their response is correct, often because the response is a few sentences and there isn't a good way to automatically assess those. Instead, we provide an answer after their response and the user compares the answer they entered (and which we can see in the SCORM report) with the answer they are shown. They can then see how close they were and adjust their learning.

The issue we're running into is that because these text entry questions are ungraded, we are not able to provide multiple attempts. Sometimes users accidentally submit something they don't intend or, because completion of the lesson **IS** graded, they are prompted by the course instructor to go back resubmit because they didn't answer the questions (provided nonsense answers instead). At the moment the only way to resubmit is to completely restart the lesson and often that wastes a lot of time.

Is there any way I can give students multiple attempts for text entry questions? Or do I need to suggest this as a new idea (frustrating, since those take a long time to go into effect and this functionality already exists for graded questions...)?

Comedian Kunal Kamra has denied reports carrying the claim from a senior Maharashtra legislative council official that he had sought an adjournment of a February 5 privilege committee hearing over what he said in a comedy show last year.  
  
Chairman of Legislative Council’s Privilege Committee Prasad Lad had on been quoted by Indian Express on February 4 as having said that Kamra apparently told the committee that he would not be able to come to Mumbai for the first mandatory hearing. “Kunal Kamra has communicated his inability to appear today. He has now been given February 17 to depose before the committee,” Lad was quoted as having said.  
  
Kamra had been in the line of fire over his stand-up show in March 2025, in which he touched upon layers of political corruption. Among those he referred to, without naming, was the Maharashtra Deputy Chief Minister Eknath Shinde. Shinde’s supporters vandalised the venue, a first information reports followed, and police went to the extent of serving notices to audience members.  
  
The Bombay high court eventually granted Kamra relief.  
  
Bharatiya Janata Party MLC Pravin Darekar had meanwhile moved a a breach-of-privilege motion in the Maharashtra Legislative Council, claiming that the remarks insulted a popular leader and amounted to a breach of the House’s privilege.  
  
Today, Kamra posted on social media, noting that he had travelled to Mumbai for the express purpose of attending the hearing, despite the short notice.
